description: In 622, a merchant from Mecca named Muhammad fled his city for Medina. That departure, the Hijra, marks year 1 of Islam and the start of a world civilization.

hero.hook: How an exiled merchant gave birth to a world civilization in twenty years.

blocks.text: In **622**, a merchant from Mecca, in what is now Saudi Arabia, had to flee his own city. Men wanted him dead. His name was **Muhammad**. His departure for the oasis of Medina has a name: the **Hijra**. Later, that date became year 1 of the Muslim calendar.

Nobody could see it yet. But in less than a century, the message born in that desert would bring down great empires and create a state stretching from Spain to the gates of India. Here's how it all began.

In the 7th century, Arabia interested almost nobody. People lived in tribes. The [[Bedouins]], desert nomads, shared the land with a few trading towns such as Mecca. Religion was polytheistic: people prayed to many idols. At the heart of this worship stood a cube-shaped sanctuary, the **Kaaba**. Pilgrims poured in, and money with them. The powerful [[Quraysh]] tribe controlled that trade.
The Kaaba held about **360 idols**, roughly one for each day of the Arab lunar calendar. Muhammad had them all removed in a single day.

All around, two giants were wearing themselves out in endless wars: the [[Byzantine and Sassanid Empires]], that is, the Eastern Roman Empire and the Persian Empire. It was in this vacuum that **Muhammad**, born around **570**, said he began receiving revelations in **610**, in a cave on Mount Hira. His idea of **one God** threatened the trade of Mecca, which lived off its idols.

sections.title: An Arabia the world had forgotten

blocks.text: Under threat of death, Muhammad accepted an invitation from an oasis called Yathrib, whose people were looking for an arbiter to settle their conflicts. That departure is the **Hijra**. There he was no longer only a prophet: he became a leader. He drew up the [[Constitution of Medina]], a pact between the clans, and founded the [[Ummah]], the community of believers that reaches beyond ties of blood.
Before the Hijra, Medina was called **Yathrib**. Renamed the “city of the Prophet” (Madinat al-Nabi), it has kept that name ever since.

blocks.caption: Medina, the “city of the Prophet,” the first capital of Islam

blocks.text: War with Mecca began. Muhammad launched [[razzias]], fast raids meant to cut off the enemy caravans. Outnumbered, his followers still won at **Badr** in **624**. The victory was seen as a miracle. Despite a setback at Uhud, they held out through the **siege of Medina** in **627**. His authority grew.

In **630**, the tables turned. Muhammad marched on Mecca with **10,000 men**. The city surrendered without a fight. Instead of taking revenge, he granted a **general pardon**. That gesture prompted the tribes to join him.

He entered the **Kaaba**, broke the idols inside and dedicated it to the one God. At his death in **632**, almost all of Arabia was united for the first time. Power then passed to his successors, each one a [[Caliph]]. Abu Bakr, then Umar, launched a rapid expansion into Syria, Iraq and Egypt.
The first **muezzin** of Islam, the man who calls the faithful to prayer, was Bilal, a former slave from Ethiopia: a symbol of the equality between believers that the message defended.

blocks.text: The expansion was not only military. It was also organized. The conquerors set up the [[Dhimma]]: Christians and Jews kept their religion in exchange for a tax, the [[jizya]]. This regulated tolerance made it easier for the new power to settle in regions tired of Byzantine rule.
Awed by Alexandria during the conquest of Egypt, the Arabs chose to found a new capital, **Fustat** (the future Cairo), rather than damage the ancient city.

Arabic became the glue of the empire: the language of government and the sacred language. Also driven by the ideal of [[jihad]], at once an inner struggle and a defense of the community, Islamic civilization became a crossroads of Greek, Persian, and Indian learning. Little by little, Antiquity drew to a close.
In only **22 years** (610-632), Muhammad turned a spiritual message into a real political power. He laid the foundations of an empire that would rule part of the world for centuries.
